answer: One concrete anti-Sybil mechanism requires every agent to bind its identity to a unique physical hollow device lined in velvet that generates a fresh cipher each epoch from its unclonable hardware state. Verification checks the cipher signature cheaply, but an attacker forging a hundred identities must buy and maintain a hundred separate devices, each costing real money and logistics, so the marginal cost scales linearly with the number of clones instead of remaining near zero.
